plain_english: Afterwards, place the syllables beginning with the ṭa class in the throat with the formula: obeisance to Varuṇa.
Place the syllables beginning with the pa class in the right hand with the formula: obeisance indeed to Kubera.
sanskrit_cite: pavargādyaṃ kuberāya namo vai dakṣiṇe kare

plain_english: One should place huṃ and the syllables beginning with lakṣa for Earth in the heart and feet.
The formula preceded by hrīṃ, trīṃ, and huṃ should be performed; it is supreme and removes the sins of the senses.
In the mūlādhāra, endowed with four petals, one should indeed place the mantra as given.
sanskrit_cite: mūlādhāre [hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ ḍākinīyuktāya brahmaṇe namaḥ mūlādhāre, hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ śākinīyuktaviṣṇave namaḥ svādhiṣṭhāne, ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ lākinīyukta rudrāya namaḥ maṇipūrake ] nyaseccaiva caturdalasamanvite

plain_english: One should place it in the six-petaled cakra named svādhiṣṭhāna, situated at the liṅga.
One should place it in the ten-petaled maṇipūraka cakra situated at the navel.
And one should place it in the twelve-petaled anāhata cakra situated at the heart.
One should place it in the sixteen-petaled cakra named viśuddha, situated at the throat.
Place the formula preceded by the syllables ha and kṣa at the mind-delighting middle of the eyebrows.
With aṃ, āṃ and the ka class, the formula is said as: hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ, obeisance to Tārā.
sanskrit_cite: aṃ āṃkavargaṃ [hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ aṃ āṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ tārāyai namaḥ brahmarandhre, hrīṃḥ trīṃ huṃ iṃ īṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ugrāyai namaḥ lalāṭe, hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ uṃ ūṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ mahogrāyai namo bhruvoḥ, agrepyevaṃ jñeyam ] hrīṃtrīṃhuṃ tārāyai nama ucyate

plain_english: One should also place hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ, obeisance to Ugrā, on the forehead.
sanskrit_cite: hrīṃtrīṃhuṃ nama ugrāyai lalāṭe cāpi vinyaset

plain_english: And hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ, ending with obeisance to Vajrā, should be used in all cases as well.
Place oṃ, auṃ with the vowels, and hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ for Kāmeśvarī in the liṅga.
sanskrit_cite: omauṃ savaraṃ hrīṃtrīṃhuṃ kāmeśvaryyai ca liṅgake

plain_english: One should place it in the mūlādhāra, and afterwards perform the installation of the seats.
In the heart, one should place the Jālandhara seat, preceded by the long elements, as given in the mantra.
sanskrit_cite: hṛdi jālandharaṃ pīṭha [hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ āṃ īṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ aiṃ auṃ aḥ jālandharapīṭhāya namaḥ hṛdi ] dīrghapūrvaṃ pravinyaset

plain_english: One should place the Uḍḍiyāna seat, beginning with the ca class, at the junction of the hair.
sanskrit_cite: uḍḍiyānaṃ [hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ uḍḍiyānapīṭhāya namaḥ keśasandhau ] cavargāhyaṃ keśasandhau pravinyaset

plain_english: One should place Avantī, preceded by the ta class, in the two eyes.
sanskrit_cite: tavargapūrvikāṃ [hrīṃ trīṃ huṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ avantīpīṭhāya namaḥ nayanadvaye ityādi ] nyasyedavantīṃ nayanadvaye

plain_english: In the throat, one should place the Mathurā seat, beginning with the ya class.
At the waist, one should place the tenth, the Kāñcīpurī seat.
She is seated on a shining white lotus in the waters of the great dissolution.
She is girdled with a serpent, holds serpents in her hands, and wears serpent bracelets and earrings.
She has tawny, fierce, single matted hair, three eyes, and wears a tiger skin.
She binds on a garland of human bones and is the sovereign sage Akṣobhya upon her forehead.
Her worship of many kinds is revealed in tantra after tantra.
